problem: Given that $y=2{x}^{e}-ln⁡x$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Sum Containing a Natural Logarithm Function
examples.worked_solution:
Taking the derivative, we have

$$
\eqalign{
			f'(x) &= \left(2\ln x+x^2-1\right)'\
			&=2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}+2x-0\
			&=\dfrac{2}{x}+2x.

}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
The derivative of the natural logarithm is the reciprocal function:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x)=\frac{1}{x}
$$

We apply our formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{7}{3}ln⁡x) \\  & =-\frac{7}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡x) \\  & =-\frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =-\frac{7}{3x}.\end{aligned}
$$
